# The standard packages, series 0.4

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill/build.py from libraries/ and `rnl catalog`. Edit those, not this file. -->

What a file of RNL 0.4 can name without writing it: the definitions its statements fill (`@AS $NAME`), the symbols its instances are drawn with, and the sets it edits. No package is used by itself: a file names the collection `rnl-std-all` in its header record, or the packages it wants one by one, and a file of 0.4 uses only packages of 0.4. A name that is not in the packages in use is an error, and `rnl check` suggests the closest one. This reference is written from the package files of the series 0.4 and from the catalog of the `rnl` command, and is in step with them.

The header record of a file that uses the whole series, the optional `rnl-std-no-labels` and the Chinese aliases (the standard 2.8, 16.2, 16.3, 16.5):

```rnl
@RNL(type="header") {
  @VERSION("0.4");
  @USE-PACKAGE(name="rnl-std-all", version="0.4");
  @USE-PACKAGE(name="rnl-std-no-labels", version="0.4");
  @USE-ALIASES(name="alias-zh", version="0.4")
}
```

| `rnl-std-fill` 0.4 | `rnl-std-basic` | The sets and rules of the automatic fill: attaches ground, supply, bias and net-label stubs to unwired pins, including the pins of virtual parts, and a port tag to every port net in $PORT_FILL_SET (10.5, 12.4, 16.3). |
| `rnl-std-functional` 0.4 | – | Behavioral models: op-amps, comparators, amplifiers, transconductors, ADC, DAC and chopper modulator, with *_SUPPLY variants carrying integer-grid vp (top) and vn (bottom) pins. |
| `rnl-std-logic` 0.4 | – | Gates, buffer, inverter, delay cell and D flip-flops. |
| `rnl-std-no-instance-labels` 0.4 | – | Hides the default labels of the instances, for a file that writes its own device labels but keeps the net names that grounds, supplies, bias marks, port tags and net labels draw (16.3). |
| `rnl-std-no-labels` 0.4 | – | Hides the default labels of the standard symbols, for a file that writes its own (16.3). |

| `rnl-std-spice` 0.4 | `rnl-std-basic`, `rnl-std-semiconductors` | The rule package of SPICE: assigns symbols to instances by element letter, by model type, and by bulk or control-negative net (16.3). |
| `rnl-std-style` 0.4 | – | The styles (9.3) and the default style rules. |

## Definitions

A definition is used as `#A(role) #B(role) @AS $DEFINITION` or `$DEFINITION @ATTACH #A(role) …` (the standard 9.4, 9.5). A role in braces, such as `{members}`, is a set: it takes any number of objects, none included. A role has a kind, which says what may fill it; parameters have defaults. Group is read from the body of the definition: *yes* with the roles whose members it makes one group, *via* `$X` with the roles it passes to a definition `$X` that makes the group, and – when it makes none (the standard 11.5; see Groups in good-drawings.md).

| `$PUSH_PULL_STAGE` | `pullup` (instance/usage), `pulldown` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: pullup, pulldown | A push-pull output stage: the output transistors only, a pull-up in series with a pull-down; their bias and the stage that drives them are not part of it. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $SERIES to ?pullup and ?pulldown. |
| `$TRANSCONDUCTOR_Z_AMPLIFIER` | `transconductor` (instance/usage), `load` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: transconductor, load | An amplifier stage: a transconductor and its load. Routes; places nothing; a group: routes shared output nets between ?transconductor and ?load. |
| `$DEGENERATED_TRANSCONDUCTOR_Z_AMPLIFIER` | `transconductor` (instance/usage), `load` (instance/usage), `degenerator` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: transconductor, load, degenerator | A degenerated amplifier stage: a transconductor, its load and its degeneration. Routes; places nothing; a group, around the group of $TRANSCONDUCTOR_Z_AMPLIFIER, which it applies to ?transconductor and ?load; routes ?degenerator. |
| `$PASS_SWITCH` | `device` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A switch that passes or blocks a signal between its two sides. Meaning only: places and routes nothing. |
| `$RESET_SWITCH` | `device` (instance) | – | – | – | A precharge, equalization or reset transistor. Meaning only: places and routes nothing. |
| `$GROUND_SWITCH` | `device` (instance) | – | – | – | A low-side switch connected to a ground net. Meaning only: places and routes nothing; asserts that a channel or path terminal of ?device lies on a net in $GROUND_NET_SET. |
| `$POWER_SWITCH` | `device` (instance) | – | – | – | A high-side switch connected to a supply net. Meaning only: places and routes nothing; asserts that a channel or path terminal of ?device lies on a net in $SUPPLY_NET_SET. |
| `$TRANSMISSION_GATE` | `pmos` (instance/usage), `nmos` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: pmos, nmos | A CMOS transmission gate, the PMOS above the NMOS. Places and routes; a group: applies $PARALLEL to ?pmos and ?nmos, aligns them in one column with ?pmos above ?nmos, and asserts complementary polarities. |
| `$TRANSMISSION_GATE_HORIZONTAL` | `pmos` (instance/usage), `nmos` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: pmos, nmos | A CMOS transmission gate drawn side by side, the PMOS on the left. Places and routes; a group: applies $PARALLEL to ?pmos and ?nmos, aligns them in one row with ?pmos on the left, and asserts complementary polarities. |
| `$MULTI_POLE_SWITCH` | `{throws}` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: throws | A switch of several throws that share one pole. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $PASS_SWITCH to ?throws, routes their shared nets and asserts that all throws meet at one shared pole net. |
| `$BOOTSTRAPPED_SWITCH` | `device` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A bootstrapped sampling switch. Meaning only: places and routes nothing; specializes $PASS_SWITCH. |
| `$SC_SAMPLER` | `{switch}` (instance/usage), `{capacitor}` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A switched-capacitor sampler: sampling switches with sampling capacitors. Routes; places nothing: routes shared nets between ?switch and ?capacitor. |
| `$CHARGE_SHARING` | `a` (instance/usage), `switch` (instance/usage), `b` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A charge-sharing network: two capacitors or capacitor banks that share charge through a switch. Routes; places nothing: routes shared nets among ?a, ?switch and ?b. |
| `$CHOPPER` | `{straight}` (instance/usage), `{crossed}` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A chopper: a bridge of four switches that reverses the polarity of a signal. Routes; places nothing: applies $PASS_SWITCH and $MATCHED, routes the bridge nets, and asserts a four-switch loop alternating between ?straight and ?crossed. |
| `$FLYING_CAPACITOR` | `capacitor` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A flying capacitor switched between clock phases. Meaning only: places and routes nothing. |
| `$CMOS_INVERTER` | `pmos` (instance), `nmos` (instance) | – | – | via `$CMOS_GATE`: pmos, nmos | A CMOS inverter, the PMOS above the NMOS. Places and routes; a group: specializes $CMOS_GATE and places ?pmos above ?nmos in one column. |
| `$CMOS_INVERTER_HORIZONTAL` | `pmos` (instance), `nmos` (instance) | – | – | via `$CMOS_GATE`: pmos, nmos | A CMOS inverter drawn side by side, the PMOS on the left. Places and routes; a group: specializes $CMOS_GATE and places ?pmos to the left of ?nmos in one row. |
| `$CMOS_GATE` | `{pullup}` (instance/usage), `{pulldown}` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: pullup, pulldown | A static CMOS logic gate: a pull-up network and a pull-down network meeting in series at the output. Routes; places nothing; a group: treats {?pullup} and {?pulldown} as two networks in $SERIES and asserts complementary polarities. |
| `$LATCH` | `{members}` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: members | A latch: a bistable core with the devices around it. Routes; places nothing; a group: routes shared nets among ?members. |
| `$INVERTER_LATCH` | `a` (instance/usage), `b` (instance/usage) | – | – | via `$LATCH`: a, b | A latch of two cross-coupled inverters. Routes; places nothing; a group: specializes $LATCH and routes the cross-coupled loop nets. |
| `$SHIFT_REGISTER` | `{stages}` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A shift register: a chain of flip-flops or latches, often drawn overlapping, with clocks seldom wired. Meaning only: places and routes nothing; no group. |
| `$DIVIDER` | `upper` (instance/usage), `lower` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A divider of two branches in series, upper and lower. Routes; places nothing: applies $SERIES to ?upper and ?lower. No group, as one half often sits inside another structure. |
| `$RESISTOR_LADDER` | `{resistors}` (instance) | – | – | yes: resistors | A ladder of resistors in series in one column, from the top down. Places and routes; a group: draws ?resistors as a $BRANCH. |
| `$RESISTOR_LADDER_HORIZONTAL` | `{resistors}` (instance) | – | – | yes: resistors | A ladder of resistors in series drawn as a row. Places and routes; a group: draws ?resistors as a $BRANCH_HORIZONTAL. |
| `$PI_NETWORK` | `shunt1` (instance/usage), `series` (instance/usage), `shunt2` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A pi network: a shunt branch, a series branch and another shunt branch. Routes; places nothing: asserts loop topology among ?shunt1, ?series and ?shunt2. No group, as neighbouring pi and T networks of a ladder often share a branch. |
| `$T_NETWORK` | `series1` (instance/usage), `shunt` (instance/usage), `series2` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A T network: a series branch, a shunt branch and another series branch. Routes; places nothing: asserts star topology among ?series1, ?shunt and ?series2. No group, as neighbouring pi and T networks of a ladder often share a branch. |
| `$LC_TANK_PARALLEL` | `inductor` (instance/usage), `capacitor` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: inductor, capacitor | A parallel LC resonant tank. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $PARALLEL to ?inductor and ?capacitor. |
| `$RLC_TANK_PARALLEL` | `resistor` (instance/usage), `inductor` (instance/usage), `capacitor` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: resistor, inductor, capacitor | A parallel RLC resonant tank. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $PARALLEL to ?resistor, ?inductor and ?capacitor. |
| `$LC_TANK_SERIES` | `inductor` (instance/usage), `capacitor` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: inductor, capacitor | A series LC resonant tank. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $SERIES to ?inductor and ?capacitor. |
| `$RLC_TANK_SERIES` | `resistor` (instance/usage), `inductor` (instance/usage), `capacitor` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: resistor, inductor, capacitor | A series RLC resonant tank. Routes; places nothing; a group: applies $SERIES to ?resistor, ?inductor and ?capacitor. |
| `$DC_FEED` | `device` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | An RF choke or bias resistor that feeds a DC supply or bias to a node. Meaning only: places and routes nothing. |
| `$DECAP` | `device` (instance) | – | – | – | A decoupling capacitor on a supply or bias node. Places: its pins in one column, so that it stands upright between its node and the rail, with the usage's own point in that column. |
| `$AC_COUPLE` | `device` (instance/usage) | – | – | – | A series coupling capacitor that passes the AC signal and blocks DC. Meaning only: places and routes nothing, as it may lie or stand. |
| `$OSCILLATOR` | `{members}` (instance/usage) | – | – | yes: members | An oscillator made of its active and resonant or delay elements. Routes; places nothing; a group: routes shared nets among ?members. |

| `$MULTIPLIER` | `in1` (net), `in2` (net), `out` (net) | – | – | – | An ideal signal-flow multiplier (out = in1 * in2), drawn with $MULTIPLIER_SYMBOL. |
| `$INTEGRATOR` | `in` (net), `out` (net) | – | – | – | An ideal continuous-time integrator, drawn with $INTEGRATOR_SYMBOL. |
| `$DISCRETE_TIME_INTEGRATOR` | `in` (net), `out` (net) | – | – | – | An ideal discrete-time integrator, drawn with $DISCRETE_TIME_INTEGRATOR_SYMBOL. |
| `$QUANTIZER` | `in` (net), `out` (net) | – | – | – | An ideal quantizer, drawn with $QUANTIZER_SYMBOL. |
| `$UNIT_DELAY` | `in` (net), `out` (net) | – | – | – | An ideal unit delay, drawn with $UNIT_DELAY_SYMBOL. |

## Symbols

A symbol is chosen by the rules of the next section, or by `@SET-SYMBOL $NAME` on an object or a set. Pins are listed by terminal with the direction a wire leaves in. The standard symbols are drawn in grid steps, y up.

## Which symbol an instance gets

The rules of `rnl-std-spice` and `rnl-std-spectre` give an instance its symbol; `rnl-std-all` brings in the first for the sections in SPICE and the second for those in Spectre, through a header record for each language (2.8, 16.3). The narrow rules come later than the broad ones and win.

### rnl-std-spice: SPICE, by the first letter of the instance's name, then by the type of its `.model`

| Selector | Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| `name="R*"` | `$RESISTOR` |
| `name="C*"` | `$CAPACITOR` |
| `name="L*"` | `$INDUCTOR` |
| `name="V*"` | `$VOLTAGE_SOURCE` |
| `name="I*"` | `$CURRENT_SOURCE` |
| `name="D*"` | `$DIODE` |
| `name="E*"` | `$VCVS_4TERM` |
| `name="G*"` | `$VCCS_4TERM` |
| `name="F*"` | `$CONTROLLED_CURRENT_SOURCE` |
| `name="H*"` | `$CONTROLLED_VOLTAGE_SOURCE` |
| `name="B*"` | `$BEHAVIORAL_SOURCE` |
| `name="S*"` | `$VOLTAGE_CONTROLLED_SWITCH` |
| `name="W*"` | `$SWITCH` |
| `name="T*"` | `$TRANSMISSION_LINE` |
| `name="O*"` | `$TRANSMISSION_LINE` |
| `name="U*"` | `$RC_LINE` |
| `type="d"` | `$DIODE` |
| `type="r"` | `$RESISTOR` |
| `type="c"` | `$CAPACITOR` |
| `type="l"` | `$INDUCTOR` |
| `type="sw"` | `$VOLTAGE_CONTROLLED_SWITCH` |
| `type="nmos"` | `$NMOS_4TERM` |
| `type="npn"` | `$NPN` |
| `type="njf"` | `$NJFET` |
| `type="nmf"` | `$NJFET` |
| `type="pmos"` | `$PMOS_4TERM` |
| `type="pnp"` | `$PNP` |
| `type="lpnp"` | `$PNP` |
| `type="pjf"` | `$PJFET` |
| `type="pmf"` | `$PJFET` |
| `type="tline"` | `$TRANSMISSION_LINE` |
| `type="nmos"` with its terminal `b` on a net of `$GROUND_NET_SET` | `$NMOS` |
| `type="pmos"` with its terminal `b` on a net of `$SUPPLY_NET_SET` | `$PMOS` |
| `name="S*"` with its terminal `cn` on a net of `$GROUND_NET_SET` | `$EXTERNALLY_CONTROLLED_SWITCH` |
| `type="sw"` with its terminal `cn` on a net of `$GROUND_NET_SET` | `$EXTERNALLY_CONTROLLED_SWITCH` |

## Sets

The sets of the packages; the fill of `rnl-std-fill` is decided by them. A file adds to them or takes from them with `@ADD-TO` and `@REMOVE-FROM`.

| Set | Package |
| --- | --- |
| `$GROUND_NET_SET` | `rnl-std-basic` |
| `$SUPPLY_NET_SET` | `rnl-std-basic` |
| `$BIAS_NET_SET` | `rnl-std-basic` |
| `$PORT_FILL_SET` | `rnl-std-basic` |
| `$GROUND_FILL_SET` | `rnl-std-fill` |
| `$SUPPLY_FILL_SET` | `rnl-std-fill` |
| `$BIAS_FILL_SET` | `rnl-std-fill` |
| `$LABEL_FILL_SET` | `rnl-std-fill` |

## Chinese aliases

`alias-zh` 0.4 gives Chinese spellings of the keywords, of the names above and of the parameters and roles of their definitions: 675 aliases, listed in `libraries/standard/0.4/alias-zh.rnl` of the repository. A file loads it with `@USE-ALIASES(name="alias-zh", version="0.4")` in the header record. Each alias reads as the standard word it stands for (16.5), so a file may mix both spellings, and the standard spellings keep working.
